name: Isthmus Peak Track
why: A steep climb to a skyline ridge on the narrow neck between Lake Hāwea and Lake Wānaka, with both lakes below and the Southern Alps behind.
book: Free. Closed for fawning from 20 November to 20 December. The car park is beside SH6 north of Lake Hāwea township, 30 minutes from Wānaka: take care parking and crossing the highway. The track crosses private farmland.
water: No water sources on the track: carry plenty.
dangers: Steep, rocky switchbacks with false summits; the top only shows once you reach the ridge.
Weather changes fast: hypothermia is a risk even in summer, and snow or low cloud can bring whiteout.
Avalanches can cross the track, usually from May into November.
Safari hunting on Glen Dene Station, especially in the March-May roar: stay visible and on the track.
turnaround: If you are not on the skyline ridge by 13:00, or cloud covers it, turn back.

points.name: Isthmus Peak Track car park, Lake Hāwea
points.note: Beside SH6 on the Lake Hāwea shore. Cross the highway; the track goes through forest and farmland to a 4WD track.

points.name: Isthmus Peak summit
points.note: 1,385 m. Lake Wānaka to the west, Lake Hāwea to the east. Return the same way: there is no public access beyond.
